name: Damage sources and the hurt cooldown
note: Falls (beyond the safe fall distance: on 1.21.8 with the move that lands, rounded down; on 1.21.4 without it, rounded up), the void, starvation, the effects' magic and wither damage, fire (in_fire), burning (on_fire), lava and magma blocks (hot_floor), drowning (the air supply, entity event 67 on 1.21.8), suffocation (in_wall), cacti, sweet berry bushes moved across and freezing in powder snow (the frozen ticks and the powder_snow slowness); fire resistance keeps fire's damage off; armor wears and reduces the damage it reduces (not the bypasses_armor tag's), resistance takes 20% a level, absorption takes damage first; damage that tires costs its exhaustion; within the hurt cooldown more damage takes only the difference, without the damage event, hurt animation, knockback or sound (client/combat); the game rules fallDamage, fireDamage, drowningDamage and freezeDamage; the damage event, the hurt sound by the damage type's effects (hurt_on_fire, hurt_drown, hurt_freeze, hurt_sweet_berry_bush), death and fall sounds for the others nearby and the velocity at the next entity update (none for drowning; 0 after a teleport or a move in a sweet berry bush), as both official servers send them
deviations: the velocity told is that of a player standing still, or at the bottom of lava, or 0 after a teleport or a move in a sweet berry bush (players hurt in the air, moving elsewhere or in water were not recorded)
the fall sound of the block landed on is not played
the hurt and death sounds' pitches come from Circuit's own draws
campfires and bubble columns' air are not modeled; the suffocating blocks are taken to be the redstone conductors (stone and glass recorded)

a magma block hurts a player standing on its edge by the nearest block under them that bears them (minecraft.wiki; not recorded); lava halves the distance fallen each tick by minecraft.wiki (not recorded)
